questions.prompt: You press Ctrl+C after the reply "Let me check the fi" has streamed. What does the step record?
options: Nothing, so the model never knows the reply started
An assistant/attempt, which the model never sees
An assistant/message with "Let me check the fi", marked interrupted
The full reply, after waiting for the stream to finish
questions.explanation: Text the person already saw is kept as an interrupted assistant message. Derived history then includes it, so the model sees what the person saw.

questions.prompt: A stream fails with a rate-limit error at the same moment the person pressed Ctrl+C. Why does the step check signal.aborted before the retry logic?
options: A stop the person asked for must never be retried
Rate-limit errors are never retried anyway
The signal must be reset before the next attempt
Retrying would duplicate the tool calls
questions.explanation: The person wants the work to stop. Checking the signal first means an abort ends the turn instead of starting another attempt.

questions.prompt: The model asked for call_1 and call_2. call_1 is running when the person cancels; call_2 has not started. What results end up in the log?
options: Only call_1 gets a result; call_2 is removed from the message
call_1 gets an error result from the stopped tool, and call_2 gets a synthetic 'aborted before it started' result
No results; the turn is marked aborted instead
Both get success results so the history stays valid
questions.explanation: Every tool call needs a matching result for the next request to be valid. The stopped tool reports its own error, and the unstarted call gets a synthetic error, as an orphaned tool call would.
